# Yánluó walks into a legal, justice & compliance firm

Somewhere right now, in a legal, justice & compliance office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Yánluó**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**Yama, the First Mortal.** Before he was a king of hell he was the first man to die: the Ṛgveda's Yama chose mortality, found the road to the other world, and became the guide and host of the fathers — honoured with songs and offerings.  Buddhism inherited him as the dharma-king who interrogates the dead: the three messengers — old age, sickness, death — are his summonses, sent to every house.

**The Fifth Tribunal.** The Chinese Ten Kings system, formed by the Tang, stations Yánluó in the fifth court — the great reckoning after the first four screenings.  There the record books are opened, the mirror of deeds is raised, and the verdict is assigned: paradise, rebirth, or the numbered hells.  One legend says he once held the first court but was demoted for leniency — even the king of the dead is audited.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

*The judge of the dead, enthroned in his courtroom with the record books of every life — wealth and rank are nothing before him.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Insurance & Protection Services

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The exact record and the final accounting; judgment as audit.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Yánluó was always going to be re-derived wherever judgment, underworld, order matters.

### Software, Cloud & Developer Infrastructure

*The immutable ledger of deeds; the audit log made sacred.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

## Not the First Rebrand

He is the supreme case of Buddhist localization: Yama became Yánluó in China, Enma in Japan (with his own mirror and the red-faced scowl of a thousand temple gates), Yeomna in Korea, and the judges of Vietnamese and Central Asian afterlives.  Daoism staffed his courts with its own celestial bureaucrats; folk religion added Mèngpó's tea and the City God as his local deputies. The office is only the latest translation.
